title: Two-way table, probability out of everyone
subtitle: Probability and conditional probability · 8 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **8 of the official questions in Probability and conditional probability are this one** — 5 Easy, 3 Medium, 0 Hard.
It is bottom-heavy, which makes it cheap points. Secure it early.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- You see a grid with row and column categories, usually with Total margins.
- The question says to select one member of the whole group at random, and it names either one trait (like 'votes for X' or 'is at least N years old') or a pair of traits ('has A but not B').

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) The denominator is the grand total in the bottom-right corner, or the sum of all cells if no total is printed.
- 2) The numerator is the row or column total for a single trait, or the one cell where the named row and column meet for a pair of traits.

sections.heading: Where Desmos fits
body: It's a table lookup and one division.
Desmos only helps you turn the fraction into a decimal to match the choices.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: The wrong answers use the right numerator over a row or column total, which answers a conditional question nobody asked.
They also use a neighbouring cell, or read 'has A but not B' as the cell for 'has A and B'.

sections.heading: You are losing these
body: Before you choose, say out loud what the question is asking for — not what you solved for.
